name: Creo
description: Hermetic Technique whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Cruthaich.

name: Intellego
description: Hermetic Technique whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Fios.

name: Muto
description: Hermetic Technique whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Atharraich.

name: Perdo
description: Hermetic Technique whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Sgrios.

name: Rego
description: Hermetic Technique whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Ceannseach.

name: Animal
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Beatach.

name: Aquam
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Uisge.

name: Auram
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Aile.

name: Corpus
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Corp.

name: Herbam
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Lus.

name: Ignem
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Teine.

name: Imaginem
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Iomhaigh.

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Inntinn.

name: Terram
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Tir.

name: Vim
description: Hermetic Form whose Gaelic name in the Loch Leglean glossary is Cumhachd.

name: Redcap
description: Messenger magus of House Mercere; Gaelic 'Teachdair' (messenger). Thomas Verus is a wandering Redcap.

name: Apprentice
description: A magus in training; Gaelic 'Foghlumach' (learner).

name: Consors
description: Companion character; Gaelic 'Caraid' (friend).

name: Covenant
description: A community of magi; Gaelic 'Comhairle' (council).

name: Custos
description: Covenant guard or servant; Gaelic 'Freiceadan' (guard).

name: Grog
description: Covenant supporter or soldier; Gaelic 'Dionadair' (supporter).

name: Turb
description: A covenant's band of grogs; Gaelic 'Comhlan' (band) or 'Buidhean' (company).

name: Magic
description: Spells and magic, rendered in Gaelic as Geasadaireachd or Druidheachd.

name: Scotland
description: The realm covered by the Loch Leglean Tribunal, settled over centuries by Broch-builders, Picts, Scots, Vikings, Britons and Saxons.

name: Lowlands
description: English in culture and law, with many English and Norman families; ruled by the Roman Church.

name: Highlands
description: Hilly, thickly wooded lands where clans rule and bow to no king; home to giants in their further reaches and to the Scottish Church's abbeys.

name: England
description: Kingdom to the south whose English and Normans are gaining control over the Scots.

name: Ireland
description: Country named in the Gaelic glossary.

name: France
description: Country named in the Gaelic glossary.

name: Rome
description: City named in the Gaelic glossary.

name: Picts
description: People who succeeded the Broch-builders in Scotland's history.

name: Scots
description: People of Scotland who succeeded the Picts; now losing control to the English and Normans.

name: Broch-builders
description: The earliest people in Scotland's history, succeeded by the Picts and Scots.

name: Vikings
description: Norse whose descendants rule large parts of the northern Highlands and the Islands.

name: Normans
description: Immigrants gaining control over the Scots; many Norman families live in the Lowlands, and demons have come with them.

name: Border lords
description: Lords between Scotland and England who will follow either king for a price.

name: King Alexander II
description: Son of William the Lion and king of Scotland, ruling from Castle Rock in Edinburgh; he joined the rebellion against King John and signed the Magna Carta.

name: William the Lion
description: Former king of Scotland, father of Alexander II.

name: King John of England
description: King of England against whom Alexander II rebelled; father of Joan.

name: Joan
description: Daughter of King John of England, betrothed to Alexander II.

name: Magna Carta
description: Charter signed by Alexander II after joining the rebellion against King John.

name: Castle Rock
description: The king of Scotland's seat in Edinburgh, where the Stone of Scone lies.

name: Edinburgh
description: City where King Alexander II rules from Castle Rock.

name: Stone of Scone
description: Stone at Castle Rock over which all Scottish kings have been crowned.

name: Lord Goulis
description: Seneschal of Scotland, rumored to be a servant of Satan; his family has held the office as a hereditary fief for three generations.

name: Satan
description: The devil, whom Lord Goulis is rumored to serve.

name: Roman Church
description: Rules the Lowlands and is making inroads into the Highlands at the expense of the native Church.

name: Scottish Church
description: Native Church with abbeys in the Highlands; it holds services in Gaelic instead of Latin.

name: Guillame de Bruyse
description: Bishop of St. Andrews and primate of the Church in Scotland.

name: St. Andrews
description: Bishopric whose bishop is primate of the Church in Scotland.

name: Gaelic
description: Language of the Highland Scots, used in Scottish Church services.

name: Pralix
description: First Hermetic wizard to come to Scotland; she pursued and battled Damhan-allaidh, and the tribunal is named for her winter camp.

name: Damhan-allaidh
description: Foe whom Pralix pursued to Scotland and fought in many battles.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: Hermetic House, many of whose original members came from Scotland.

name: Loch Leglean Tribunal
description: Tribunal of Scotland formed in 817, named for Pralix's winter camp; a quarter of its magi belong to no covenant.

name: Schism War
description: Hermetic war during which, in 1008, three Loch Leglean covenants tied to House Diedne were destroyed.

name: House Diedne
description: Hermetic House closely associated with three Loch Leglean covenants destroyed in 1008.

name: Pact of Crun Clach
description: Agreement of 1189 that reduced Loch Leglean magi's direct involvement in mortal affairs.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The Hermetic order; its Loch Leglean magi tend to side with non-Hermetic neighbors against mainland magi.

name: Crun Clach
description: A Lowland covenant and one of the three largest in Loch Leglean.

name: Clan Mac Gruagach
description: A Highland covenant and one of the three largest in Loch Leglean.

name: Horsingas
description: A Saxon covenant and one of the three largest in Loch Leglean; home of the quaesitor Whitburh Frithowebba.

name: Aonaranan
description: Loch Leglean magi tied to no covenant who keep their tribunal voting rights.

name: Whitburh Frithowebba
description: Magus of Horsingas Covenant and the only quaesitor in the Tribunal.

name: Quaesitor
description: Hermetic investigator; Whitburh Frithowebba is the only one in Loch Leglean.

name: Thomas Verus
description: Wandering Redcap, the only member of House Mercere whose route includes Scotland.

name: House Mercere
description: House of the Redcaps; Thomas Verus is the only member whose route includes Scotland.

name: Faeries
description: Common in Scotland; Highland faeries are usually solitary, strange and dangerous, while more humanlike faeries live in knowes.

name: Knowe
description: Hollow hill where the more tolerant, humanlike faeries live.

name: Rade
description: A faerie ride or procession.

name: Gruagachan
description: Magicians from an ancient, non-Hermetic tradition.

name: Order of Odin
description: Wizards found in the northern Islands.

name: Demons
description: Arrived with Norman and English immigrants but are still less common in Scotland than elsewhere.

name: Giants
description: Live in the further reaches of the Highlands.

name: Stoorworm
description: A form of water wyrm living in the seas off Scotland's north coast.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The game setting; demons are more common across it than in Scotland.

name: Islands
description: Scottish isles ruled by Viking descendants, where the Order of Odin is found.
